newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index edges up led by Biotika.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index edges up led by Biotika.

text.p: Major Slovak stocks closed mostly stronger in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with heavy gains to drug maker Biotika pushing the SAX index up 1.79 points to 187.77.
Biotika, which is Slovakia's major pharmaceutical firm, led Tuesday trading with 16,510 shares matched, rising 143 crowns to close at 925.

Brokers said that such a large package of Biotika shares was traded because of a previously agreed deal which had only now been registered on the market and that the move did not indicate a fundamental development in the issue's price.
Brokers said the market now seemed to be undervalued and that they expected low prices to attract foreign investors within the next few weeks.

"Prices have fallen to attractive levels, and we think that those investors now focusing on Poland, Hungary or Russia, may turn their attention to Slovakia when those markets stop their current growth," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
He said that the inflow of foreign investors would increase the market's liquidity and push the market on upward trend.
Oil refiner Slovnaft gained 20 crowns to close at 800, but traded only 30 shares. Dealers said Slovnaft share holders may be prepared to sell to potential investors at around 850 crowns.
Steel producer VSZ closed up three crowns at 645, and brokers said the share was now the most liquid issue on the market with strong demand expected to push its price even higher.
Overall volume fell to 261,263 shares, from 517,630 traded on Monday, and turnover decreased to 197.04 million crowns from 392.48 million.
